name: Needle cupping

card.summary: Suction cupping applied over acupuncture needles, used in traditional Chinese medicine and by some athletes for muscle tension and recovery that support training.
card.note: Leaves circular bruise marks; burns and skin damage are documented with fire cupping.

quick.overview:
Needle cupping combines two traditional Chinese medicine techniques: acupuncture needles are inserted and a suction cup is placed over the area. Practitioners and some athletes use it for muscle tension, pain and recovery, which feeds into being able to train and move comfortably.

Reviews of cupping in general describe the research as limited or of poor quality for most conditions, with low to moderate evidence for musculoskeletal pain. Studies specifically of the combined technique are mostly small clinical reports and protocols in the Chinese-language literature.
quick.how: A practitioner inserts needles and then places a cup, often glass or plastic with a pump, over the site so suction draws the skin up. Some devices combine the two in one apparatus, including patented magnetic-needle cups. Sessions leave round marks that fade over days.
quick.risks: Cupping can cause bruising, discolouration, burns (with fire cupping), blisters and infection risk. Needling adds the general risks of acupuncture. Some people with skin conditions such as eczema or psoriasis may find them worsened.

lead: Needle cupping is the practice of applying a suction cup over an inserted acupuncture needle, or over a site being needled, combining two techniques of traditional Chinese medicine [1]. Practitioners use cupping to relieve muscle tension and pain, and athletes who adopt it describe it as part of recovery between workouts [1].

Chinese clinical reports describe combined treatments such as plum-blossom needling, cupping and electroacupuncture for conditions like traumatic myositis ossificans of the elbow, and meta-analyses and protocols group cupping with other acupuncture-type methods for chronic fatigue syndrome and COVID-19 [3][4][5]. Patents also exist for needle-type and magnetic-needle cupping devices [6][7].

chain: Suction and needling over tight muscle
Reported relief of tension and soreness
angle.text: Lifters and athletes use cupping, sometimes with needling, for tight areas such as the back or traps in the hope of easier training. The visible round marks are a side effect.

paras: In cupping, a cup creates suction on the skin, traditionally by heating the air inside it, and is left in place or moved over oiled skin. Practitioners attribute effects to improved circulation and to dispelling stagnation in traditional Chinese medicine terms [1]. Cupping is often performed alongside acupuncture [1]. Device patents describe single apparatus that integrate a magnetic needle with a suction cup [6][7].

Lifters on training forums mention cupping for muscle tension; one user wrote that it helped leg and back tension during rehab and later preferred dry needling because it leaves fewer marks [8]. Athletes drew wide attention to cupping marks at the 2016 Olympics [1].

A 2009 meta-analysis of randomized trials of acupuncture-related treatments for chronic fatigue syndrome included cupping among its search terms [3]. A 2020 protocol proposed a systematic review of external traditional Chinese medicine, including cupping, for COVID-19 [4], and a 2011 report described a combined plum-blossom needle, cupping and electroacupuncture treatment for elbow myositis ossificans [5]. No trial specifically testing needle cupping for appearance or recovery in athletes was found.
Reviews of cupping alone report poor study quality for most conditions, and low to moderate evidence for musculoskeletal pain whose benefit may not differ from placebo [1].
Documented effects of cupping include bruising, skin discolouration, burns with fire cupping, blisters, scarring and pain. Marks have occasionally been mistaken for signs of child abuse [1].

timeline.event: Chinese utility patents for magnetic-needle cupping devices are filed [6][7].
Cupping marks on Olympic athletes receive worldwide media attention [1].
